title: Test the reported pro-female evaluation bias in Jev at scale
description: A public write-up (urasmutlu.dev, 'A First Look at Jev', September 2026) scored 34 hand-written male/female/they scenario triples on competence, likability and hireability with Jev's score primitive and found the female variant scored higher on 33 of 34 pairs (mean absolute delta 0.155 on a 0-4 scale), largest on assertive and emotional scenarios (e.g. pounding the table, -0.46 hireability). Our gendered-language pre-registration (2a384ef) predicts the opposite for loaded words. Test it on real bios at n = 2,000 with a floor: evaluative questions (competence, likability, promotability) alongside our occupation-assignment questions, pronoun and name cues, the singular-they variant as a third arm (it is itself a cue, not a neutral baseline), and the ask-twice noise floor. Report both directions: a boost for women on evaluation and a push toward lower-status roles on assignment can coexist.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Feature: Evaluation and assignment gender bias measured together
  Scenario: Evaluative questions on real bios
    Given 2,000 real bios answered by an engine as written, with pronouns swapped, and with singular they
    When I score competence, likability and promotability
    Then the study reports the female-minus-male shift and the they-minus-male shift with 95% intervals against the ask-twice floor
  Scenario: Direction is reported, not assumed
    Given the same bios scored on an occupation-assignment question
    When both scores are reported side by side
    Then a positive evaluation shift for women and a stereotype-ward assignment shift can both be detected in one engine

right_now_summary: The team is designing a 2,000-bio test of gender effects on evaluations and job assignments.
